title: FHP Identity Model
description: Defines the identity and reference model for all entities in the Fair Hiring Protocol. All IDs are opaque UUID v4 values. No ID may be derived from PII. This document is the canonical reference for ID formats used across all FHP schemas.

fhp_id.description: A UUID v4. Opaque, globally unique, never derived from PII.

candidate_id.description: Identifies a candidate. Issued by the FHP platform at registration. Stable for the lifetime of the account. Never reused.

company_id.description: Identifies a registered company. Issued at company onboarding. Stable for the lifetime of the account.

job_id.description: Identifies a single job brief. Generated when a job brief is first saved (even in draft status). Immutable once issued.

match_id.description: Identifies a single match event between one candidate and one job. Generated by the matching engine at the time of scoring. Immutable. Referenced in explanations, traces, and appeal records.

trace_id.description: Identifies a single pipeline execution trace. One trace is produced per match_id per pipeline run. Immutable.

appeal_id.description: Identifies a candidate appeal against a match outcome. Generated when an appeal is submitted.

audit_id.description: Identifies a fairness audit record. Generated by the nightly fairness computation job.

description: An FHP entity reference — used to validate any object that carries FHP identifiers.

id_lifecycle.description: Rules governing the lifecycle of all FHP identifiers.
rules: IDs are issued by the FHP platform, never by clients.
IDs are never recycled or reassigned after deletion.
Deleted entity IDs are tombstoned: the ID is retained in the identity store with status='deleted' and a deletion timestamp, but all associated data is purged.
IDs are never exposed in URLs as path parameters in external-facing APIs — use opaque tokens instead.
Cross-entity relationships are always expressed as references (e.g. match contains candidate_id + job_id), never by embedding the full entity.

privacy_model.description: How identity and PII are separated.
rules: The candidate_id is the only cross-system identifier for a candidate.
PII (name, email, phone) lives in the identity service only, never in the matching engine, trace store, or fairness computation outputs.
The matching engine operates exclusively on candidate_id — it never receives PII.
Explanations generated for employers reference match_id and skill ontology IDs only — no candidate PII until the candidate consents to contact.
Audit and fairness records reference candidate_id and demographic cohort labels only — never individual PII.

id_format.rationale: UUID v4 is random, unguessable, globally unique without a central registry, and carries no information about the entity it identifies — satisfying the opaqueness requirement.
